result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-030 (walk-in registration at the door; GitHub issue #33; depends_on REQ-029; third and final requirement of Phase 6) at commit 5f40393, branch feature/WF02-REQ-030. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report yaml, or any prior gate's summary as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md in full (all 13 sections, AC1-AC6, all 6 open questions) then read the shipped implementation directly: domain/walkin.ts (387 lines -- parseWalkinArgs/validateWalkinFields §2, normalizePhoneForMatching §3, decideWalkinOutcome's 7-row first-match-wins table §5, commitWalkin's transactional write §6, the render/re-parse pair §7) and handlers/walkin.ts (256 lines -- the 4 handlers §8). Confirmed the code matches the design line-for-line: decideWalkinOutcome implements the exact 7-step table in the exact stated order; commitWalkin opens one transaction, does a FOR UPDATE fresh read of the events row, resolves/creates the person inside the SAME transaction as the phone lookup, re-evaluates seatsLeft fresh every call (never trusts a value from an earlier tap), and writes at most one UPDATE/INSERT + one writeAuditLog call per outcome branch; every writeAuditLog payload in both write branches is exactly {eventId, source} or {eventId, previousAdmission, source} -- phone is never a key, structurally; requireOrganizerForChapter (never requireEventStaffForEvent) gates all three of the command/confirm/override steps in handlers/walkin.ts, re-authorizing fresh at each tap per §4/§8.2 step 4/§8.3. 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, the same 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx:11, Nav.tsx:10) unrelated to this diff -- matches TEST-RUNNER exactly. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js 16.3.2/Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432; container did not exist yet this session -- created fresh via `docker compose up -d`), ran `DATABASE_URL=... npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly), then `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the repo root: 31 files / 308 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches TEST-RUNNER's reported count exactly (308/308). 3. Independent re-verification with my own fresh fixtures (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req030.ts and apps/bot/scratch-rv-req030-qr.ts -- written, run, then deleted; git status confirmed clean before and after both), calling the domain functions directly, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's/TEST-RUNNER's committed test files' exact fixtures, tgId bands, or event/chapter data (own tgId bands 977_500_001-977_600_002, own chapters/events/phone values): - AC1 (abandon-at-consent, own fixture Zhanna Amanova/Nomad Robotics/+998977123456): confirmed the command-parsing/validation path produces a confirm message echoing all 3 fields verbatim, and confirmed commitWalkin is never invoked anywhere in that path (by construction/code-reading, reinforced empirically: users/profiles/registrations row counts identical before/after, and the organizer's OWN profiles row deep-equal (JSON.stringify, all columns) before vs. after) -- PASS. - AC5 (own phone value +998911119999, checked against real audit rows AND real captured console/log output): ran commitWalkin for real, then queried audit_log directly -- no row's payload text contains the raw phone or its digit-stripped form, and no payload has a "phone" key. Additionally intercepted console.log/warn/error around a second live commitWalkin call (not a static grep -- actual runtime output capture) and confirmed my own phone value never appears in any captured line -- PASS, and this is a stronger check than a static grep alone (which TEST-RUNNER already also did, zero log/console call sites in the two files). - Cross-context forgery (own two-chapter fixture, organizer A/chapter A vs. organizer B/chapter B, own tgIds 977_500_003/977_500_004): calling requireOrganizerForChapter directly with organizer A's real tgId against chapter B's event's real chapterId returns ok:false; the same call with organizer B's own tgId against their own chapter's event returns ok:true -- confirms the authorization gate (the one and only thing standing between a forged tap and commitWalkin in handlers/walkin.ts's re-derived-per-tap design) rejects a cross-chapter identity regardless of what callback_data/message text a forged dispatch might carry, matching TEST-RUNNER's own full-handler-dispatch cross-context forgery case at the handler level -- PASS. 4. Phase-6 coherence sanity check (task step 6), verified empirically with two dedicated scratch scripts, not by code-reading alone: a walk-in-created registration (admission=admitted, checked_in_at set, check_in_method='manual', source='walkin') was created via commitWalkin, then (a) checked in AGAIN via REQ-028's toggleCheckIn -- did not throw, correctly returned kind:'undo' and cleared checked_in_at (identical behavior to any other already-checked-in registration, walk-in-sourced or not; re-toggling restored the admitted+checked-in state cleanly), and (b) re-running the walk-in command for the SAME person/event via commitWalkin again correctly returned 'already-checked-in' with no throw and no duplicate row. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE TASK'S STATED PREMISE: the design (§6.2 step 9) and the shipped code both DO issue a real qr_token via generateQrToken() on every admit-and-check-in write, including a walk-in's -- a walk-in-created row is NOT left without a valid QR token as the task's step 6 assumed. I verified this directly (queried the row's qr_token column: non-null, non-empty) and then additionally scanned that walk-in's own real qr_token through REQ-029's actual performQrCheckIn: it did not throw, correctly returned kind:'already-checked-in' (no double check-in), and left check_in_method='manual' and checked_in_at byte-identical -- i.e. the QR path correctly detects and reports the prior manual check-in without overwriting it, and there is no 'no valid QR to scan' case at all for a walk-in row; the coherence property task step 6 asked about holds by a wider margin than assumed. All three check-in entry points (walk-in manual-equivalent, REQ-028 manual toggle, REQ-029 QR scan) share and interpret checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method/admission consistently with no double-write, no error, and no divergent interpretation. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat lists exactly the design-doc-listed files (domain/walkin.ts new, domain/user.ts/profile.ts extended, handlers/walkin.ts new + its two committed test files, i18n/en.ts+ru.ts+types.ts, index.ts, the design doc, the test spec, ISS-0026, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. git grep -in 'TODO\|FIXME\|XXX' across domain/walkin.ts, handlers/walkin.ts, domain/user.ts, domain/profile.ts, the i18n files, index.ts: zero matches. git status --porcelain clean before and after this handoff (both my scratch scripts removed after use). Schema: confirmed no migration files were added in this diff and db/schema.ts has zero diff -- matches the design's §0 'no change needed' conclusion, independently re-confirmed (not just re-read) by direct inspection of the live schema during my own fixture runs (chapterId nullable-tgId uniqueness, profiles nullable columns, qr_token/source/checkInMethod columns all behaved exactly as §0's table states). 6. docs/agents/requirements.yaml staleness check: REQ-030's entry (line 1525) still reads status: pending, which is correct and NOT stale at this point in the pipeline -- DOC-UPDATER (Step 6, which has not yet run) is the step that flips it to done. 7. Filed-issue judgment: ISS-0020 (MAJOR, REQ-018's staff.ts assignment-notification blocked-user gap) -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts` returning EMPTY that it is genuinely untouched by this diff and correctly out of scope. ISS-0026 (MINOR, tg_id range collision between checkinQr.forgery.test.ts and walkin.db.test.ts, both 942_000_000+): read the issue file directly -- it is a LATENT risk, not a present false-pass. Its own description states the collision has not caused an observed failure because both files currently run serialized under --no-file-parallelism (each file's counter only increments within that file's own run, so no two files ever allocate tg_ids concurrently against the shared unique constraint today); I independently confirmed this by running the full 308-test suite myself twice under --no-file-parallelism with 0 failures both times, and specifically re-ran the two implicated files' full history of prior runs's own passing status is consistent with serialized execution -- the collision would only manifest under a FUTURE change (re-introduced file-level parallelism, or a shared tg_id-pooling fixture), which is exactly what the issue is filed to flag pre-emptively. It does not affect the correctness of any currently-passing test, including the 308 in this run's own suite. Neither ISS-0020 nor ISS-0026 should block this release. Every other filed issue (ISS-0013 through ISS-0025) is unrelated to REQ-030's own surface, per the same reasoning REQ-029's own release validation already established for the ones filed before this run; no new issue was filed against REQ-030 itself by any gate (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's issues: [], TEST-RUNNER's issues: [], both confirmed by direct read). Overall: every independent check -- lint, build, the full 308-test suite from the repo root (freshly stood-up scratch Postgres), my own AC1 fixture with a column-level organizer-profile check, my own AC5 fixture with both an audit-row query AND a real captured-console-output check, my own cross-context forgery fixture at the authorization-primitive level, and my own two-script Phase-6 coherence proof spanning all three check-in entry points (walk-in/manual/QR) -- agrees with all prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present, no schema/migration changes. This closes Phase 6 (REQ-028 manual + REQ-029 QR + REQ-030 walk-in check-in system) with all three entry points confirmed mutually coherent.
